reconcile.note: Gill explains Phoenicia was anciently called Canaan, so Matthew's Canaanite and Mark's Syrophoenician name the same woman differently.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Davies and Allison read Matthew's replacement of Mark's contemporary Syrophoenician with the archaic Canaanite as a deliberate theological rewriting, not a mere synonym.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: W. D. Davies and Dale C. Allison, A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on the Gospel According to Saint Matthew, Vol. 2 (ICC) (1991).

sides.snippet: Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely demonized!
sides.verseText: Behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders, and cried, saying, \"Have mercy on me, Lord, you son of David! My daughter is severely demonized!\"

sides.snippet: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
sides.verseText: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
